title: Fitness Function & Generational Goals
lede: The mathematical foundation that quantifies evolutionary success, rewards beneficial behaviors, and steers generational adaptation.
formula: Fitness Score = (Time Survived * W_Time) + ((Resources Gathered / 40) * W_Resource) + (Kills * W_Kills) + (Distance Traveled * W_Distance) + (Events Survived * W_Events)

weights.name: W_Time
weights.description: Primary survival baseline. Every turn survived grants consistent reward.

weights.name: W_Resource
weights.description: Normalized resource consumption (per 40 points of hunger/thirst quenched).

weights.name: W_Kills
weights.description: Significant predatory payoff rewarding carnivore competitive dominance.

weights.name: W_Distance
weights.description: Exploration incentive discouraging static camping on safe tiles.

weights.name: W_Events
weights.description: Resilience bonus for enduring environmental disasters and local hazards.

components.name: Time Survived
components.rationale: The foundational survival metric. Animals that balance metabolic drain against replenishment live longer and establish a high baseline score.

components.name: Resources Gathered
components.rationale: Normalized by 40 (the quantity restored by one feeding or drinking action), directly rewarding proactive foraging over passive starvation.

components.name: Predatory Kills
components.rationale: Crucial for carnivores and aggressive omnivores. A heavy 50-point weight balances the severe physical risks of active combat.

components.name: Distance Traveled
components.rationale: Penalizes motionless turtling. A modest 0.2 weight encourages map exploration without incentivizing erratic pacing.

components.name: Events Survived
components.rationale: Rewards evasive and adaptive reflexes when environmental crises strike, promoting resilient gene lines.

generationalMilestones.description: Initial elimination of suicidal movement patterns. Animals learn to correlate positive food/water sensor activations with eat/drink motor actions.
Animals prioritize nourishment only when hunger or thirst drops below critical thresholds, conserving vital energy.
Organisms actively identify environmental threats (fire, floods) in their Moore neighborhood and execute evasion maneuvers.
Carnivores stalk herbivore trails; herbivores master evasion loops and defensive terrain positioning.
